entries.title: Proof of Estimate: an on-chain crowd forecast
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with practice SOL (about 0.1 SOL).

Complete [NameGen](/lessons/c4-comets-todor-edward-andrei/) or already understand per-wallet PDAs — Proof of Estimate is the next Stage 1 step on the [learning path](/lessons/path/). Some comfort reading Rust `u16`/`u64` arithmetic helps for the underflow exercise.
learning_objectives: Follow a program-owned mint whose authority is a PDA, and a user account that is created on the first instruction.
See a stake move from a user's token account into an escrow, as a CPI to the Token Program.
Recompute a weighted running average, and fix an underflow when a range is reversed.

entries.title: Picassol: a 200×200 pixel canvas where every pixel is an account
prerequisites: A Phantom (or Solflare) wallet set to Solana Devnet, and enough practice SOL from [faucet.solana.com](https://faucet.solana.com) for the estimated costs (about 0.05 SOL is typical for this lesson). Faucet availability and timing vary; faucet access is not graded.

If you are new to Solana, complete Foundations Lessons [001](/lessons/first-transaction/)–[007](/lessons/protecting-state-transitions/) first (start at Lesson 001). If you already understand execution vs commitment, accounts, and safe recovery habits, you may start here as Stage 1 on the [learning path](/lessons/path/).
learning_objectives: Derive a Program Derived Address from seeds you choose — here, a pixel's x and y as single bytes.
Explain why each pixel is its own 14-byte account, and what those 14 bytes hold (discriminator, position, colour, bump).
Tell create (`init`) from update (re-derive the same PDA from stored fields), and find the `PixelChanged` event in the logs.

entries.title: TrustLock: a dead man's switch for SOL
prerequisites: Two Phantom accounts (owner and beneficiary) and about 0.2 Devnet SOL in the owner's.
Complete [gree](/lessons/gree/) or equivalent PDA/CPI familiarity — TrustLock is the next Stage 1 step on the [learning path](/lessons/path/). Clock sysvar and escrow close are new here.
learning_objectives: Use the Clock sysvar to enforce a deadline the frontend cannot override.
Follow SOL into an escrow PDA and back out, and see `close` return the rent to a chosen wallet.
Tell the two guards apart: the beneficiary cannot claim early, and the owner cannot check in after the deadline.

entries.title: gree: mint a 1-of-1 NFT with Metaplex metadata in one instruction
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with practice SOL (about 0.1 SOL — minting creates several accounts).
Complete [Proof of Estimate](/lessons/poe-solana/) or equivalent CPI familiarity — gree is the next Stage 1 step on the [learning path](/lessons/path/).
learning_objectives: Follow a single instruction that mints one token and, in the same transaction, makes a CPI to Metaplex to attach name, symbol and URI.
Derive the metadata PDA the same way Metaplex does, and confirm the mint's supply is 1 and its mint authority is empty.
See why a program signs a CPI as a PDA (`invoke_signed`) when it is the mint authority.

entries.title: Web3 Splitter: split token payments by percentage (and learn PDA signing from two real bugs)
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and a little SOL. You will also need to be comfortable with token accounts.
[gree](/lessons/gree/) (CPI to the Token Program, PDA signing) and [Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/) (missing account checks).
learning_objectives: Follow an SPL-token vault that splits deposits by percentage, with a PDA as the token-account owner.
Reproduce, from the recorded transactions, why `claim` only works for the creator (a seeds / signer mismatch).
See a second, related bug in how the PDA is asked to sign, and write a local test that proves the fix.

entries.title: OrbOracle: a stake-weighted, time-decayed price oracle
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with about 0.1 practice SOL, plus a 0-decimal weight token mint for Create/Deposit.
Complete [Novengrid staking](/lessons/colosseum/) — OrbOracle closes [stage 3](/lessons/path/#stage-3). This is an oracle feed other programs could read, not a sentiment market like sentient.send.
learning_objectives: Run a stake-weighted price oracle: submit a price, see the aggregate, and watch old submissions fade with time.
Recompute the aggregate from the recorded submissions, and find a submitter's reward.
See a lock release and a quorum that may not be a real percentage.

entries.title: sentient.send: a winner-takes-all sentiment market where the side with the most SOL wins
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with about 0.1–1+ practice SOL (create needs ≥1 SOL stake).
Complete Stage 2 ending at [NAIM](/lessons/naim/) — sentient.send opens [stage 3](/lessons/path/#stage-3). [TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) (Clock, close) is the closest Stage 1 escrow parallel.
learning_objectives: Open a winner-takes-all market with a deadline, several sides, and a pool that the winning side splits by stake.
Compute a payout from the recorded amounts before you claim it, and see where fees go.
Hit a 32-byte seed limit, and a tie, on purpose.

entries.title: CipherVault: a SOL multisig vault (and the account checks it forgot)
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with about 0.1–1.1 practice SOL for the creator. A second wallet is useful for the other-owner steps.

Complete Stage 1 ending at [Gifter escrow](/lessons/gifter-escrow/) — CipherVault opens [stage 2](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Elective lessons on missing `has_one` ([Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/), [UniProof](/lessons/chinesepowered-solana-cypherpunk/)) help the audit section but are not required to walk propose → approve → execute.
learning_objectives: Walk a multisig: propose, approve, execute when the threshold is reached.
Find the account checks that are missing at `execute` and at `approve`, each proven on devnet.
Fix the leftover-accounts path so a proposal can only move funds from its own vault, and only once.

entries.title: Novengrid SOL staking: a time-locked SOL vault that pays per-second rewards
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with about 0.1 practice SOL.

Complete [sentient.send](/lessons/sentient-send/) — Novengrid staking is next on [stage 3](/lessons/path/#stage-3). [TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) (Clock) helps. Bring a calculator for the reward exercise.
learning_objectives: Follow a time-locked SOL vault whose rewards grow every second, from the Clock.
Predict a reward from the recorded rate and elapsed time, and see what re-staking does to unclaimed rewards.
Spot an overflow at a realistic stake size, and the way principal and rewards share one balance.

entries.title: stakes.wtf: stake a token for gov tokens, grow their value with bribes, unstake into linear vesting
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet, plus whatever test token the app mints for you.
[Colosseum](/lessons/colosseum/) (staking, time) and [gree](/lessons/gree/) (token CPIs). This is the densest token-economics lesson.
learning_objectives: Stake a token, receive gov tokens, and watch an exchange rate move when a bribe is added to the pool.
Unstake into a linear vest, and compute how much is withdrawable at a given time.
Find why a UI bribe didn't land where the label said, and repair a Create Pool path that fails.

entries.title: Votara: on-chain DAO proposals with one vote per wallet, quorum and an approval threshold
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 devnet SOL.
Stage 1, especially [TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) (Clock) and [PulseFund](/lessons/pulsefund-sol/) (one PDA per wallet). This is the first lesson in [stage 2](/lessons/path/#stage-2).
learning_objectives: Read a DAO flow: register, create a proposal (counter-numbered PDA), vote once, finalize after the period.
See a `has_one`-style authority check at finalization, and a 'one vote per wallet' rule enforced by a PDA.
Spot a quorum that is compared to a raw count instead of a percentage, and a proposal id you can block.

entries.title: Barn / OpenGrants: grant programs with milestone reviews and capped payouts
prerequisites: Two wallets (sponsor and developer) and about 0.05 SOL in the sponsor's.
Stage 2 up through [Votara](/lessons/votara/) (counters, roles). This is the most structured state machine so far.
learning_objectives: Walk a tree of counter-numbered PDAs: profile → program/project → grant → milestone, each derived from its parent and a count.
See a payout cap enforced in one line: `paid_out + amount ≤ approved_amount`.
Find, and fix, `reject_grant_milestone` calling `accept_milestone()` — proven on devnet, where the 'rejected' milestone is Accepted.

entries.title: CS2 Prediction Market: YES/NO tokens on constant-product curves, resolved by an admin
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 SOL. You will create your own market (trading is whitelist-gated to the creator by default).
The rest of the path, especially [sentient.send](/lessons/sentient-send/) (markets) and [Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/) (vault PDAs). This is the last lesson: curves, fees and a shared vault.
learning_objectives: Trade YES and NO tokens on two constant-product curves, and recompute a recorded buy and sell from the reserves.
See a single global vault holding every market's SOL, and a 0.2% LP fee that is credited to reserves but never taken from the buyer (proven on devnet).
Name the two missing instructions — claim, and a withdraw that actually transfers — and the 1232-byte `create_market` limit.

entries.title: PulseFund: one-PDA-per-wallet SOL crowdfunding with an admin-only withdraw
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and about 0.3 devnet SOL (the 9,000-byte campaign costs about 0.046 SOL of rent, and Contribute sends 0.2 SOL).
Lesson 1, [Picassol](/lessons/picassol-hackathon/), or the same idea: you know what a PDA is and how seeds make an address unique.
learning_objectives: Create a PDA seeded only by a wallet, so each wallet can have exactly one campaign.
Move SOL into a program-owned account with a System Program transfer, and take it back out by editing lamports directly.
Use the rent-exempt minimum as a withdrawal floor, and spot a frontend that talks to the wrong account.

entries.title: UniProof: university credentials as PDAs, with registrar and dean sign-off
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and about 0.05 SOL.
[Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/) immediately before this: you have just seen a missing `has_one` on a payee. Here the same idea is about *who may set a flag*.
learning_objectives: Compare two instruction structs side by side: `issue` and `revoke` locked with `has_one`, and `SignCredential` with a signer that is never compared to a role.
Use a counter-numbered PDA (`["credential", university, n]`) and walk a university's credentials.
Explain a seed mismatch: a university stored a different authority than the key it was derived from, and became unusable.

entries.title: Friendstake: peer-to-peer bets with a named judge and a PDA-signed vault
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and about 0.05 SOL. With one wallet, name yourself as opponent and judge, as the click test did.
[TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) (escrow, close) and [PulseFund](/lessons/pulsefund-sol/) (SOL in and out). This lesson is about *who the program pays*.
learning_objectives: Follow a two-account design: a program-owned Bet PDA for state, and a system-owned vault PDA that holds only SOL and signs transfers with its seeds.
See `has_one` correctly lock `take` and `settle` to the named opponent and judge.
Find the three missing payee checks, each proven on devnet with a measured SOL amount.

entries.title: DeVos: on-chain elections with an allow-list, named positions and a close-to-tally step
prerequisites: Phantom on devnet and a little devnet SOL.

[Votara](/lessons/votara/) immediately before this: you have just seen on-chain voting with a VoteRecord PDA per (proposal, voter). Here one Election account holds the allow-list, the positions and the votes, and grows with realloc. This is still [stage 2](/lessons/path/#stage-2).
learning_objectives: Create a named election PDA, with space computed from maxima, that starts closed and holds positions, candidates, the allow-list and every vote in one account.
Walk the recorded path: add positions (each starts with Abstain), add candidates, open, vote once per position, close, and store winners with get_winner.
Spot that tally_votes only writes the program log, that toggle_election has no finished state, and that the hosted UI never opens the election or adds voters.

entries.title: Gifter escrow: accounts, token swaps and refunds
prerequisites: Phantom on Devnet with a little practice SOL. On the 13 Nov 2026 hosted build the token dropdown filled after connect.

Complete [TrustLock](/lessons/trustlock/) immediately before this: you have just seen a SOL escrow with a Clock deadline. Here the vault is an SPL-token ATA, and there is no expiry. This is the last lesson in [stage 1](/lessons/path/#stage-1).
learning_objectives: Create an escrow PDA and deposit mint A into an associated-token vault the PDA owns, naming mint B and a price.
Refund: the vault signs a transfer_checked back to the maker and both accounts close; an outsider cannot refund.
Tell a completed take (33yMgZzA… on 45C1bSkF…) from the earlier abort (ck53TqoU… on 6Z5cvVUc…).

entries.title: NameGen: one display-name PDA per wallet
prerequisites: A Phantom or Solflare wallet on Solana Devnet with practice SOL.
Complete [Picassol](/lessons/picassol-hackathon/) or already understand PDAs from seeds — NameGen is the next Stage 1 step after Picassol on the [learning path](/lessons/path/).
learning_objectives: Create a per-wallet PDA seeded ["user", authority].
Write and clear a fixed-size 64-byte name field on that PDA.
Explain why another wallet cannot edit your PDA (ConstraintSeeds).

entries.title: MandateKey: on-chain spending limits for AI agent wallets
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL (create_mandate pays rent).
Complete [CipherVault](/lessons/ciphervault/) or equivalent Stage 2 start — MandateKey is next on the [learning path](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with PDAs and Anchor accounts.
learning_objectives: Create a mandate PDA seeded by owner, agent and id, and read it back from devnet.
Explain the pay check order and why a revoked mandate cannot spend.
Revoke a mandate as the owner.

entries.title: Trust Protocol: on-chain identity bonds for autonomous AI agents
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL (initialize pays rent for two PDAs).

Complete [MandateKey](/lessons/mandatekey/) or equivalent Stage 2 progress — Trust Protocol is next on the [learning path](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with PDAs, Anchor init constraints, and SPL mints.
learning_objectives: Explain what initialize writes to the protocol-config and insurance-pool PDAs.
Derive those PDAs from the documented seeds and the lab program id.
State why a second initialize fails and what is still needed before register_agent.

entries.title: ZeroAI: on-chain crypto prediction snapshots with Pyth
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL (initvault and initgames pay rent).

Complete [Trust Protocol](/lessons/trust-protocol/) or equivalent Stage 2 progress — ZeroAI is next on the [learning path](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with Anchor accounts and Pyth price-feed accounts.
learning_objectives: Create a vault of Pyth feed addresses and read it back from devnet.
Derive the games PDA and initialise it.
Explain why addgame can succeed with closeprice all zeros.

entries.title: Oculus: rolling spending limits for AI agent wallets
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL (init_policy pays rent). A second agent keypair is useful for check_spend.
Complete [ZeroAI](/lessons/zeroai/) or equivalent Stage 2 progress — Oculus is next on the [learning path](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with PDAs and Anchor account constraints.
learning_objectives: Create a policy PDA seeded by an agent pubkey and read it back.
Explain the check_spend budget and pause checks.
Pause and close a policy as the owner.

entries.title: AgentX: on-chain lifecycle for autonomous AI agents
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL.
Complete [Oculus](/lessons/oculus/) or equivalent Stage 2 progress — AgentX is next on the [learning path](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with PDAs and Anchor constraints.
learning_objectives: Initialise (or fetch) the registry PDA.
Register, activate and deactivate an agent.
Explain why execute_task requires Active status and the registry authority as oracle.

entries.title: NAIM: on-chain .agent names for AI agents
prerequisites: A wallet on Devnet with a little practice SOL.
Complete [AgentX](/lessons/agentx/) — NAIM closes [stage 2](/lessons/path/#stage-2). Comfort with PDAs and Anchor init constraints.
learning_objectives: Explain what initialize writes to the config PDA.
Derive that PDA from the documented seeds.
State why register_name cannot run until init_token_config exists.

entries.title: Guild Protocol: on-chain agent labor market
prerequisites: naim
learning_objectives: Initialise a guild config
Register a bonded agent
Read agent state and name the rejected errors

entries.title: QVAC Marketplace: register an inference provider
prerequisites: guild-protocol
learning_objectives: Register a provider PDA
Update provider fields
Name the rejected errors

entries.title: AgentTrust: issue and revoke an on-chain agent credential
prerequisites: qvac-marketplace
learning_objectives: Issue a credential PDA
Revoke it
Name AlreadyRevoked

entries.title: Agenc Protocol: initialise the coordination config
prerequisites: agenttrust
learning_objectives: Initialise protocol config
Name InvalidDisputeThreshold
Explain the ProgramData remaining account

entries.title: Forge Agent Bounty: initialise the bounty marketplace
prerequisites: agenc-protocol
learning_objectives: Initialise the marketplace
Read total_bounties

entries.title: Hydra: register a root agent in a hierarchical registry
prerequisites: forge-agent-bounty
learning_objectives: Initialise the registry
Register a root agent
Name NameTooLong

entries.title: Agent Bazaar: register an on-chain agent identity
prerequisites: hydra
learning_objectives: Initialise the protocol
Register an agent
Name InvalidFee

entries.title: AgentVault
prerequisites: agent-bazaar
learning_objectives: Initialise global state
Register two agents and list a service
Escrow and accept a task
See why complete_task payout fails

entries.title: Orrery
prerequisites: agentvault
learning_objectives: Initialise config as upgrade authority
Register a provider
Open a settle-token payment channel

entries.title: Reddi Escrow
prerequisites: orrery
learning_objectives: Register an agent
Lock SOL in a program-owned escrow
Release the escrow to a payee

entries.title: AgentEscrow
prerequisites: A Phantom or Solflare wallet on Solana Devnet with practice SOL and the lesson mint if required.
Comfortable with [accounts and authority](/lessons/accounts-ownership/) or equivalent.
learning_objectives: Create and fund an SPL-token escrow vault PDA for an agent job.
Explain the provider start → submit → payer confirm sequence.
Identify which accounts hold funds before and after confirmation.

entries.title: Pact Escrow
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Basic familiarity with SPL token accounts.
learning_objectives: Locate the pact escrow PDA and the tokens it controls.
Walk the create → fund → release (or cancel) flow on the hosted app.
Read a successful transaction and name the instruction that moved funds.

entries.title: SolAgents Agentic Commerce
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice SOL/tokens for the lesson mint.
Read [instructions and programs](/lessons/instructions-programs/) or equivalent.
learning_objectives: Identify buyer, seller, and settlement accounts in the commerce program.
Execute one recorded purchase/settlement path on Devnet.
Explain what evidence proves the payment settled.

entries.title: Lattice Escrow
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Understanding of PDA seeds from [Picassol](/lessons/picassol-hackathon/) or Foundations.
learning_objectives: Derive or locate the escrow PDA used by Lattice.
Fund the escrow and observe locked token balances.
Explain which condition unlocks release vs reclaim.

entries.title: TrustRail Pipelines
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Comfortable reading multi-instruction transactions.
learning_objectives: Identify the pipeline accounts and their roles.
Submit one pipeline action on Devnet and find it on Explorer.
Explain how later steps depend on earlier account state.

entries.title: Veedor Settlement
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds and the lesson mint.
Understanding of [accounts and authority](/lessons/accounts-ownership/).
learning_objectives: Create a job escrow PDA and fund it with SPL tokens.
Submit evidence and identify the verifier’s role in release.
Distinguish locked funds from released funds in account state.

entries.title: Atlantid Vault + Escrow
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Basic program/instruction literacy from Foundations 003 or equivalent.
learning_objectives: Identify the Atlantid program ID and relevant PDAs.
Complete one guided transaction on Devnet.
Match program logs to the instruction you intended.

entries.title: Allowance
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Familiarity with signer vs owned accounts.
learning_objectives: Explain what an allowance account authorises.
Perform one allowance set or spend on Devnet.
Show how a spend beyond the limit is rejected (or cite recorded rejection).

entries.title: EscrowAgent
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
Accounts and authority basics.
learning_objectives: Create or fund an EscrowAgent vault and name its authorities.
Complete one release or refund path on Devnet.
Explain who can move funds at each state.

entries.title: Agent Court
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds and the lesson mint.
Understanding of escrow authorities and dispute outcomes.
learning_objectives: Deposit SPL tokens into a two-agent escrow PDA.
Explain how a Release verdict unlocks a claim.
Locate the claim transaction and name who received funds.

entries.title: Covenant
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds.
PDA and authority basics.
learning_objectives: Identify covenant accounts and the release condition.
Fund a covenant and observe locked balances.
Walk one release or cancel path with Explorer evidence.

entries.title: Otomat
prerequisites: A Devnet wallet with practice funds and the lesson mint.
Comfortable with multi-instruction transactions (Foundations 004 or equivalent).
learning_objectives: Open a channel PDA and lock tokens for payer→payee.
Explain why the Ed25519 pre-instruction matters for settle.
Settle a signed check and verify balances after settlement.

entries.title: Authorise and verify a transaction
prerequisites: A practice wallet on Solana Devnet; no prior Solana required.
learning_objectives: Separate submission, execution result, and commitment.
Reject a wallet request that does not match intention.
Verify a transfer on the intended network before claiming success.

entries.title: Accounts, ownership, and authority
prerequisites: Lesson 001 — Authorise and verify a transaction (or equivalent).
learning_objectives: Identify an account’s owner program vs authorities in its data.
Predict who must sign an update.
Explain why the wrong signer fails.

entries.title: Instructions and programs
prerequisites: Lesson 002 — Accounts, ownership, and authority.
learning_objectives: Name the program and accounts an instruction touches.
Predict state change before sending.
Verify observed accounts match the prediction.

entries.title: Multi-instruction transactions and atomicity
prerequisites: Lesson 003 — Instructions and programs.
learning_objectives: Identify multiple instructions in one transaction.
Predict all-or-nothing outcomes.
Relate atomicity to fees when execution fails.

entries.title: Failure diagnosis and recovery
prerequisites: Lesson 004 — Multi-instruction transactions and atomicity.
learning_objectives: Separate rejection, simulation, execution, and commitment failures.
Avoid blind resubmit after unresolved status.
Reconcile before a corrected attempt.

entries.title: Reliable client state
prerequisites: Lesson 005 — Failure diagnosis and recovery.
learning_objectives: Label observed vs draft vs pending vs outcome.
Avoid treating a failed refresh as proof of non-execution.
Preserve drafts across detected conflicts.

entries.title: Program-enforced expected revisions
prerequisites: Lesson 006 — Reliable client state.
learning_objectives: State what an expected revision check protects.
Distinguish client races from program-enforced checks.
Choose review-before-resubmit after conflicts.
